text: A developer needs to have records with specific field values in order to test a new Apex class. What should the developer do to ensure the data is available to the test?

options.text: Use SOQL to query the org for the required data.
Use Test.loadData() and reference a CSV file in a static resource.
Use Anonymous Apex to create the required data.
Use Test.loadData() and reference a JSON file in Documents.

explanation: Test.loadData(sObjectType, 'resourceName') inserts records from a CSV file stored as a static resource, so the test controls the exact field values and doesn't rely on org data. Querying existing data fails because tests can't see org data by default. Records created in Anonymous Apex are real org data, so the test still wouldn't see them, and Test.loadData() only reads CSV static resources, not JSON files in Documents.
reviewNote: Restored garbled options ('Use SOQE to carry the app...', 'Test::ListSize(s)') to the standard wording with Test.loadData().

text: Universal Containers (UC) wants to lower its shipping cost while making the shipping process more efficient. The Distribution Officer advises UC to implement global addresses to allow multiple Accounts to share a default pickup address. The developer is tasked to create the supporting object and relationship for this business requirement and uses the Setup Menu to create a custom object called "Global Address". Which field should the developer add to create the most efficient model that supports the business need?

options.text: Add a master-detail field on the Global Address object to the Account object.
Add a master-detail field on the Account object to the Global Address object.
Add a lookup field on the Global Address object to the Account object.
Add a lookup field on the Account object to the Global Address object.

explanation: Exam key: a master-detail field on Account to Global Address. Note: standard objects such as Account can't be on the detail side of a master-detail relationship, and making Account a detail would force every Account to have an address. Because many Accounts share one Global Address, the documented model is a lookup field on Account pointing to Global Address. A field on Global Address pointing to Account would let each address link to only one Account.
reviewNote: Key appears incorrect: Account can't be the detail in a master-detail; correct model is a lookup on Account to Global Address (D).

text: A developer deployed a trigger to update the status__c of Assets related to an Account when the Account's status changes and a nightly integration that updates Accounts in bulk has started to fail with limit failures. [Code snippet in document] What should the developer change about the code to address the failure while still having the code update all of the Assets correctly?

options.text: Change the getAssetsToUpdate method to process all Accounts in one call and call it outside of the for loop that starts on line 02.
Add a LIMIT clause to the SOQL Query on line 16 to limit the number of Assets queried for an Account.
Move all of the logic to a @future method that queries for and updates the Assets and call it from the trigger.
Perform the SOQL query for Assets on line 14 and iterate over the assets list in the for loop on line 15.

explanation: Exam key: adding a LIMIT clause. Limiting the Assets per query does not fix the root cause (a SOQL query executed once per Account inside the loop) and would leave some Assets unupdated, which breaks the requirement. Note: the documented best practice is to bulkify the helper so getAssetsToUpdate processes all Accounts in one call outside the loop, querying Assets once. Moving logic to @future just shifts the same per-record queries into another transaction.
reviewNote: Key appears incorrect: a LIMIT clause would skip Assets; bulkifying getAssetsToUpdate (A) is the standard answer. Also the source omits the code snippet ('[Code snippet in document]').

text: Which code in a Visualforce page and/or controller might present a security vulnerability?

options.text: <apex:outputText value="{!get.userinput}" escape="false"/>
<apex:outputText value="{!get.userinput}" escape="true"/>
<apex:outputText value="{!$CurrentPage.parameters.userinput}" escape="true"/>
<apex:outputText value="{!$CurrentPage.parameters.userinput}" escape="false"/>

explanation: Rendering a URL parameter from $CurrentPage.parameters with escape="false" outputs raw, attacker-controlled input into the page, which is a classic reflected cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability. Keeping escape="true" (the default) HTML-encodes the value and neutralizes injected script. The {!get.userinput} variants reference a controller value rather than raw request input, so the URL-parameter version with escaping disabled is the clear vulnerability.

text:
A developer identifies the following triggers on the 'Expense__c' object: 
deleteExpense, applyDefaultsToExpense, validateExpenseUpdate;
The triggers process before delete, before insert, and before update events respectively. Which two techniques should the developer implement to ensure trigger best practices are followed?

options.text: Create helper classes to execute the appropriate logic when a record is saved.
Remove the before insert and before update triggers and use Flows for the delete action.
Combine all three triggers into a single trigger on the 'Expense__c' object that includes all events.
Maintain all three triggers on the 'Expense__c' object, but move the business logic out of the trigger definition.

explanation: Best practice is one trigger per object, because the execution order of multiple triggers on the same object is not guaranteed; combining them into a single trigger covering all events fixes that. Logic should then live in helper (handler) classes so the trigger stays thin, testable and reusable. Keeping three triggers retains the ordering problem, and swapping triggers for Flows is not a trigger best practice.

text: Universal Hiring uses Salesforce to capture job applications. A Salesforce administrator created two custom objects; 'Job__c' acting as the master object, 'Job_Application__c' acting as the detail. Within the 'Job__c' object, a custom multi-select picklist, 'Preferred_Locations__c', contains a list of approved states for the position. Each 'Job_Application__c' record relates to a Contact within the system through a master-detail relationship. Recruiters have requested the ability to view whether the Contact's Mailing State value matches a value selected on the 'Preferred_Locations__c' field, within the 'Job_Application__c' record. Recruiters would like this value to be kept in sync if changes occur to the Contact's Mailing State. What is the recommended tool a developer should use to meet the business requirement?

options.text: Roll-up summary field
Apex trigger
Formula field
Record-triggered flow

explanation: Exam key: formula field. A formula would stay in sync automatically, but formula INCLUDES() requires a text literal as its second argument, so it cannot compare a multi-select picklist against another field such as Contact__r.MailingState. Note: the commonly documented answer is a record-triggered flow, which can evaluate the match and update the Job Application whenever the Contact changes, declaratively. A roll-up summary only aggregates child records and does not fit.
reviewNote: Key appears incorrect: INCLUDES() cannot compare a multi-select picklist to a field value; a record-triggered flow is the standard answer (yesterday's bank keyed it).

text: Which two are phases in the Aura application event propagation framework?

options.text: Emit
Default
Bubble
Control

explanation: Aura application events propagate through three phases: capture, bubble and default. Bubble passes the event from the source component up to the root, and default notifies all remaining handlers once capture and bubble finish (unless propagation was stopped). Emit and Control are not propagation phases in the Aura framework.

text: A developer needs to allow users to complete a form on an Account record that will create a record for a custom object. The form needs to display different fields depending on the user's job role. The functionality should only be available to a small group of users. Which three things should the developer do to satisfy these requirements?

options.text: Create a Custom Permission for the users.
Create a Lightning web component.
Add a Dynamic Action to the Users' assigned Page Layouts.
Create a Dynamic Form.
Add a Dynamic Action to the Account Record Page.

explanation: Exam key: Custom Permission, Lightning web component and Dynamic Form. A Custom Permission restricts the feature to a small group, and a Dynamic Form shows different fields based on visibility rules such as the user's role. Note: the standard answer replaces the LWC with a Dynamic Action on the Account Record Page, which surfaces the create action only for users with the Custom Permission and is fully declarative. Dynamic Actions are configured on Lightning record pages, not page layouts.
reviewNote: Key appears incorrect: the commonly cited answer is A, D, E (Custom Permission, Dynamic Form, Dynamic Action on the Account Record Page); a custom LWC is not needed.

text:
A developer created this Apex trigger that calls MyClass.myStaticMethod: 
trigger myTrigger on Contact (before insert) {
    MyClass.myStaticMethod(trigger.new);
}
The developer creates a test class with a test method that calls MyClass.myStaticMethod directly, resulting in 81% overall code coverage. What happens when the developer tries to deploy the trigger and two classes to production, assuming no other code exists?

options.text: The deployment passes because both classes and the trigger were included in the deployment.
The deployment fails because no assertions were made in the test method.
The deployment fails because the Apex trigger has no code coverage.
The deployment passes because the Apex code has the required >75% code coverage.

explanation: Deploying to production requires at least 75% overall coverage and at least 1% coverage for every trigger. Because the test calls MyClass.myStaticMethod directly and never inserts a Contact, myTrigger never runs and has 0% coverage, so the deployment fails despite 81% overall coverage. Missing assertions are poor practice but do not block deployment, and simply including the files does not satisfy the trigger coverage rule.

text: A developer created a new after insert trigger on the Lead object that creates Task records for each Lead. After deploying to production, an existing outside integration that inserts Lead records in batches to Salesforce is occasionally reporting total batch failures being caused by the Task insert statement. This causes the integration process in the outside system to stop, requiring a manual restart. Which change should the developer make to allow the integration to continue when some records in a batch cause failures due to the Task insert statement, so that manual restarts are not needed?

options.text: Use the Database method with allOrNone set to false.
Remove the Apex class from the integration user's profile.
Use a try-catch block after the insert statement.
Deactivate the trigger before the integration runs.

explanation: Database.insert(tasks, false) performs partial-success DML: valid Tasks are inserted and failures are returned in SaveResult objects instead of throwing an exception that rolls back the whole batch. A try-catch placed after the insert cannot catch anything, and catching the exception would still lose all Tasks. Removing class access or deactivating the trigger just disables the required functionality.

text: A developer is working on a project to import data from an external system into Salesforce. The data contains sensitive information that should not be visible to all users in Salesforce. What should the developer do to ensure that the data is secure?

options.text: Use the Salesforce CLI to import the data and set up user permissions to restrict access to sensitive data.
Use the Apex Data Loader to import the data and write Apex code to handle security and access control.
Use a third-party tool to encrypt the sensitive data before importing it into Salesforce.
Use the Data Import Wizard to import the data and set up field-level security to restrict access to sensitive fields.

explanation: Field-level security is the declarative control for hiding specific sensitive fields from users who should not see them, and the Data Import Wizard respects the platform security model during import. Writing Apex to enforce access duplicates what FLS already provides, and encrypting data externally before import makes it unusable in Salesforce without solving visibility. Generic user permissions do not target individual fields the way FLS does.

text: A developer is implementing an Apex class for a financial system. Within the class, the variables 'creditAmount' and 'debitAmount' should not be able to change once a value is assigned. In which two ways can the developer declare the variables to ensure their value can only be assigned one time?

options.text: Use the static keyword and assign its value in a static initializer.
Use the final keyword and assign its value when declaring the variable.
Use the final keyword and assign its value in the class constructor.
Use the static keyword and assign its value in the class constructor.

explanation: In Apex, a final variable can be assigned only once, either in its declaration or in an initializer/constructor; after that, any reassignment is a compile error. That makes declaring it final with an inline value, or final with assignment in the constructor, the two valid approaches. The static keyword only makes the variable belong to the class rather than an instance; on its own it does not prevent the value from being changed later.

text: How is a controller and extension specified for a custom object named "Notice" on a Visualforce page?

options.text: <apex:page standardController="Notice" extensions="myControllerExtension">
<apex:page controller="Notice__c" extensions="myControllerExtension">
<apex:page = "Notice" extends="myControllerExtension">
<apex:page controllers = "Notice, myControllerExtension">

explanation: A Visualforce page uses the standardController attribute for the object's standard controller and the extensions attribute for one or more extension classes, which is the pattern in the keyed option. Note that for a custom object the value must be the API name, standardController="Notice__c". The controller attribute is for custom controller classes, not objects, and extends or controllers are not valid apex:page attributes.
reviewNote: Keyed option uses standardController="Notice"; for a custom object the API name Notice__c is required, so the option is only correct in pattern.

text: A developer is integrating with a legacy on-premise SQL database. What should the developer use to ensure the data being integrated is matched to the right records in Salesforce?

options.text: External ID field
Formula field
External Object
Lookup field

explanation: An External ID field stores the legacy system's unique key on the Salesforce record, is indexed, and can be used by upsert operations to match incoming rows to existing records and avoid duplicates. External Objects surface external data through Salesforce Connect without importing it, which is a different integration pattern. Formula and lookup fields do not provide a record-matching key for integration.

text: A developer has identified a method in an Apex class that performs resource intensive actions in memory by iterating over the result set of a SOQL statement on the account. The method also performs a DML statement to save the changes to the database. Which two techniques should the developer implement as a best practice to ensure transaction control and avoid exceeding governor limits?

options.text: Use the Database.savepoint method to enforce database integrity.
Use the System.Limit class to monitor the current CPU governor limit consumption.
Use the @ReadOnly annotation to bypass the number of rows returned by a SOQL.
Use partial DML statements to ensure only valid data is committed.

explanation: A savepoint (Database.setSavepoint() with Database.rollback()) gives transaction control, letting the method restore the database state if processing fails partway. The Limits class (for example Limits.getCpuTime() against Limits.getLimitCpuTime()) lets the code monitor consumption and stop before hitting a limit. @ReadOnly is only allowed in specific contexts and prevents DML, and partial DML controls which rows commit but does nothing for limits.

text: A developer is using Agentforce Dev Assistant and noticed that the output from their prompt resembles proprietary code. Which model training considerations should the developer be aware of when utilizing the extension?

options.text: Dev Assistant can reference the developer's prior prompts to generate output in near real time.
Dev Assistant can reference other developers' code and train the model in near real time.
Dev Assistant generated output resembles the code that was used to train the model.
Dev Assistant anonymized PII data in customer code that was used to train the model.

explanation: Generative code models produce output that reflects the patterns of the code they were trained on, so suggestions can resemble existing code and must be reviewed before use. Salesforce states that customer code and prompts are not used to train the model in real time, which rules out the options about learning from the developer's or other developers' prompts and code. Customer code is not used for training, so the anonymized-PII option does not apply.

text: Which two Agentforce limitations should a developer consider when building an agent?

options.text: Version control is supported for agents.
Inbound messages sent via messaging channels have character limits.
Custom actions that reference an Apex class or flow support only primitive data types.
The Agent API has a 90-second timeout.

explanation: Agentforce documents limits on the size of inbound messages that come through messaging channels, so long customer messages have to fit within the character limits. Custom actions that call Apex or flows are documented as supporting primitive data types for inputs and outputs, so complex objects must be simplified. Version control support is a capability rather than a limitation. Note that the same question is keyed differently as label 203 in this document.
reviewNote: The source prints this question twice with different keys (A, B and B, C); this copy's key (primitive data types + messaging character limits) matches the commonly cited answer.

text:
A developer receives an error when compiling the following code: 
switch on sObject {
    when Account a, Contact c {
        System.debug('account ' + a);
        System.debug('contact ' + c);
    }
    when null {
        System.debug('null');
    }
    when else {
        System.debug('default');
    }
}
What is the error?

options.text: Switch statements cannot contain multiple when values.
There is incompatible variable binding.
Only one sObject type per when block can be used.
There is an unexpected token 'Contact'.

explanation: When switching on an sObject, each when clause can declare only a single type with a bound variable, such as when Account a. The parser does not expect a second type after the comma, so the compiler reports an unexpected token at Contact. Multiple comma-separated literal values are allowed for other switch types, so that option is wrong; the restriction is a syntax error, reported as an unexpected token rather than a binding error.

text:
A developer is asked to write helper methods that create test data for unit tests. 
01: public TestUtils {
02:
03:     public static Account createAccount() {
04:         Account act = new Account();
05:         //...set some fields on act...
06:         return act;
07:     }
08:     //...other methods...
09: }
What should be changed in the TestUtils class so that its methods are only usable by unit test methods?

options.text: Add @IsTest above line 03.
Add @isTest above line 01.
Change public to private on line 01.
Remove static from line 03.

explanation: Annotating the class with @isTest makes it a test utility class: its code can only be called from test methods, it does not count against the org's code size limit, and it is excluded from coverage calculations. Putting @IsTest on the method would turn it into a test method rather than a reusable helper. Making the class private or removing static does not restrict usage to tests.

text:
Refer to the following Apex code: 
Integer x = 0;
do {
    x = x + 1;
    x++;
} while (x < 1);
System.debug(x);
What is the value of x when it is written to the debug log?
explanation: A do-while loop always runs its body at least once. In that first pass x = x + 1 sets x to 1 and x++ sets it to 2; the condition x < 1 is then false, so the loop exits and System.debug writes 2. The loop does not run a second time, so 3 and 4 are not possible, and 1 ignores the second increment.
reviewNote: Source code contained LaTeX-style artifacts ('Integer $x=0;$', '$x=x+1;$', 'while $(x<1)$'); restored to plain Apex.

text: Which two actions may cause triggers to fire?

options.text: Cascading delete operations
Changing a user's default division when the transfer division option is checked
Renaming or replacing a picklist entry
Updates to FeedItem

text: What are two characteristics related to formulas?

options.text: Formulas can reference themselves.
Formulas are calculated at runtime and are not stored in the database.
Fields that are used in a formula field can be deleted or edited without editing the formula.
Formulas can reference values in related objects.

explanation: Formula fields are read-only values calculated when the record is read, so they are not stored in the database. They can use cross-object references to pull values from related parent objects (for example Account.Industry on a Contact). A formula cannot reference itself, and a field referenced by a formula cannot be deleted until it is removed from the formula.

Build an account assignment rule.

text: A developer is configuring the Einstein Trust Layer for Universal Containers. Which three features are used to keep the company safe while exploring generative AI solutions?

options.text: Zero data retention policy
Safe Prompt Generation
Dynamic grounding with secure data retrieval
Data masking
Sharing rules

It also provides toxicity detection and audit trails. "Safe Prompt Generation" is not a named Trust Layer feature, and sharing rules are part of the general record-access model rather than the Trust Layer.

text: Which aspect of Apex programming is limited due to multitenancy?

options.text: The number of records returned from database queries
The number of active Apex classes
The number of records processed in a loop
The number of methods in an Apex class

explanation: Because all tenants share the same infrastructure, the Apex runtime enforces governor limits on shared resources, such as a maximum of 50,000 records returned by SOQL queries per transaction. There is no governor limit on the number of active classes, methods in a class, or iterations over records in a loop (beyond CPU time). That makes query rows the aspect limited by multitenancy.

text: Which two scenarios require an Apex method to be called imperatively from a Lightning web component?

options.text: Calling a method with the click of a button
Calling a method that makes a web service callout
Calling a method that is not annotated with cacheable=true
Calling a method that is external to the main controller for the Lightning web component

explanation: @wire runs reactively when the component loads or parameters change, so invoking Apex in response to a user action such as a button click must be done imperatively. Wired methods must also be @AuraEnabled(cacheable=true); any method without cacheable=true (for example one that performs DML) can only be called imperatively. Callouts can be made from either style, and any @AuraEnabled class can be imported, so being outside a main controller is irrelevant.

text: Universal Containers decides to use exclusively declarative development to build out a new Salesforce application. Which three options should be used to build out the database layer for the application?

options.text: Custom objects and fields
Triggers
Flows
Roll-up summaries
Relationships

explanation: The database (data model) layer is built declaratively with custom objects and fields to store data, relationships such as lookups and master-detail to connect objects, and roll-up summary fields to aggregate child data on parents. Flows are declarative but belong to the business logic layer, and triggers are Apex code, so they don't fit an exclusively declarative data layer.
